recognize_zh: 周邊血液中兩個比紅血球大的原始淋巴球：核質比高、染色質細緻、胞質極少，上方細胞核有明顯缺刻（nuclear notch），下方細胞可見小核仁；需以流式細胞儀確認 T 細胞系（cCD3）。
features: Two medium-sized blasts, about 1.5–2 times the diameter of a red cell
High N:C ratio with scant pale blue cytoplasm
Upper cell with a nuclear notch/indentation and denser chromatin
Lower cell with finely dispersed chromatin and a faint nucleolus
No cytoplasmic granules or Auer rods; background normocytic red cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two circulating blasts of medium size with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, scant agranular cytoplasm and finely dispersed chromatin; one has a nuclear indentation and the other a faint nucleolus. No granules or Auer rods are seen. The background red cells are unremarkable. Findings are consistent with circulating lymphoblasts; lineage assignment as T-lymphoblastic leukemia requires flow cytometry (cytoplasmic CD3, CD7, TdT).

ddx.vs: B-lymphoblasts are morphologically indistinguishable and are separated by expression of CD19, CD79a and CD22 instead of cytoplasmic CD3.
Myeloblasts may lack granules but are MPO or CD13/CD33/CD117 positive rather than cCD3 positive.
Reactive lymphocytes have condensed chromatin and more abundant basophilic cytoplasm that hugs adjacent red cells.
Sézary cells have condensed, cerebriform chromatin and are TdT and CD34 negative.
